judgments.reason: The absence of an exclusive venue clause is an omitted protection, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "FRUENDS"
judgments.reason: “FRUENDS” is an obvious misspelling of “FRIENDS” and does not alter the listed alternative source of funds.

neg3.clause_name: Disclosure of Fee as Finance Charge
neg3.label: NEGATIVE

judgments.title: Spelling error: "Trath"
judgments.reason: “Federal Trath in Lending Act” unmistakably identifies the Truth in Lending Act despite the spelling error.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: finance charge in disclosure section
judgments.reason: Lowercase “finance charge” is used descriptively and remains clear; capitalization is not necessary to identify the concept.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "Trath"
judgments.reason: The misspelled statutory title still unmistakably refers to the federal Truth in Lending Act.

judgments.title: Entire Agreement Clause Lacks Acknowledgment of Related Documents
judgments.reason: The integration clause is expressly limited to the agreement between the customer and PLS, so it does not facially supersede the separate loan agreement with the Lender.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "maticr"
judgments.reason: “Maticr” is an obvious misspelling of “matter” and does not alter the integration clause’s scope.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "maticr"
judgments.reason: “Maticr” is plainly “matter” in context and does not affect the entire-agreement clause’s scope.

judgments.title: Corrupted acknowledgment text
judgments.reason: The heavily corrupted acknowledgment language obscures the certification that the customer received, read, and retained the documents.

judgments.title: Corrupted agreement reference
judgments.reason: The malformed text mechanically prevents the acknowledgment from clearly identifying the referenced agreement or disclosure document.

judgments.title: Garbled cancellation notice reference
judgments.reason: The garbled phrase obscures the operative acknowledgment concerning the number of cancellation notices received.

judgments.title: Broad information sharing authorization
judgments.reason: The authorization is broad, but “any information” expressly conveys breadth rather than an uncertain scope requiring construction.

judgments.title: Bankruptcy warranty may be unenforceable
judgments.reason: The future-intent bankruptcy warranty may be unenforceable as a matter of public policy, but its wording is clear and internally consistent.

judgments.title: Formatting artifacts in acknowledgment opening
judgments.reason: The subsection label and central acknowledgment phrase are mechanically corrupted in the signature certification.

judgments.title: Formatting artifacts in disclosure statement reference
judgments.reason: The corruption prevents the acknowledgment from clearly identifying the first referenced disclosure document and the Credit Services Agreement.

judgments.title: Formatting artifacts in cancellation notice reference
judgments.reason: The garbled numbering and transition text mechanically obscure the acknowledgment that two cancellation notices were received.

judgments.title: No Cap on Information Sharing Duration
judgments.reason: “Any subsequent services” has an uncertain temporal and transactional boundary and could encompass either related future services or an indefinite series of services.

judgments.title: Total of Payments Figure Appears Incorrect
judgments.reason: The stated Total of Payments is mechanically inconsistent with both the payment schedule and the disclosed principal-plus-finance-charge total.

judgments.title: Payment Count Appears Garbled ("LO" Instead of "10")
judgments.reason: “LO payments” is a mechanical corruption of the payment count and leaves an operative repayment term facially defective.

judgments.title: Finance Charge Components Do Not Sum Correctly
judgments.reason: The stated components total $559.15, not the disclosed $561.15 Finance Charge, creating an intrinsic arithmetic error.

judgments.title: Ambiguous CAB Fee Refund Language
judgments.reason: The phrase “for the final period” is genuinely unclear as to whether proration covers only the last installment period or the entire remaining term.

judgments.title: Annualized CAB Fee Rate Disclosure May Create Regulatory Risk
judgments.reason: Prominence of the annualized CAB-fee rate may create regulatory or litigation exposure, but it does not create ambiguity or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "Pinance"
judgments.reason: “Pinance” is an obvious misspelling of “Finance” and does not alter the disclosed concept.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "Finanee"
judgments.reason: “Finanee Charge” is plainly recognizable as “Finance Charge” and does not create a genuine interpretive issue.

judgments.title: Capitalization error: "Followed"
judgments.reason: Mid-sentence capitalization of “Followed” is a stylistic error that does not change the payment schedule’s meaning.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "abtain"
judgments.reason: “Abtain” is an obvious misspelling of “obtain” and does not affect the early-payment provision’s meaning.

judgments.title: Inconsistent usage: amount finaneed
judgments.reason: “Amount finaneed” is readily understood as “amount financed”; the spelling and capitalization do not create a genuine uncertainty about the fee base.

judgments.title: Total of Payments appears incorrect
judgments.reason: The stated Total of Payments is mechanically inconsistent with the installment schedule and the sum of Amount Financed and Finance Charge.

judgments.title: CAB fee refund limited to prorated daily basis for final period only
judgments.reason: “For the final period” is genuinely uncertain as to whether the CAB-fee refund covers only the last installment period or all remaining time after early payoff.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "abtain"
judgments.reason: “Abtain” is plainly “obtain” and does not alter the early-payment term.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Payday Installment
judgments.reason: “Payday installment” is a descriptive product label rather than an operative capitalized defined term, and the loan’s amount and schedule are separately stated.

judgments.title: LOC Reimbursement Interest Rate May Be Inadequate
judgments.reason: Whether 10% adequately compensates PLS is a commercial issue; the specified rate is unambiguous.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "rec"
judgments.reason: The broken word in the operative request for issuance of the LOC is a mechanical corruption, even though “request” is the evident intended word.

judgments.title: Stacked return item fees from both CAB and Lender
judgments.reason: The contract clearly states separate return-item obligations to CAB and the Lender; alleged unfair stacking is a substantive issue, not ambiguity.

judgments.title: LOC Described as "Irrevocable" but Later Made Revocable
judgments.reason: The operative description of the LOC as “irrevocable” conflicts with the later provision stating that it is automatically revoked upon timely cancellation.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: lender
judgments.reason: In context, each lowercase reference to “the lender” plainly means the identified loan lender; capitalization does not create a genuine alternative referent.

judgments.title: Inconsistent usage: irrevocable LOC
judgments.reason: “Irrevocable” is simply an adjective modifying the defined abbreviation LOC; it need not itself be separately defined.

judgments.title: CAB disclaims responsibility for verifying lender statements
judgments.reason: The documentary-presentment standard and disclaimer of accuracy verification are express; the issue seeks a different substantive duty.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "shal!"
judgments.reason: “Shal!” is an obvious typographical rendering of “shall” and does not affect the LOC’s stated lack of further effect.

judgments.title: Spelling error: "nol"
judgments.reason: “Nol” is plainly “not” in context and does not create a reasonable alternative reading of the CAB’s verification disclaimer.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: Lender
judgments.reason: The surrounding references to the LOC beneficiary and the customer’s loan make clear that lowercase “lender” means the identified Lender.

judgments.title: Incomplete text in DEFAULT section
judgments.reason: The corruptions “th4+-Agreement” and “yr~ader” mechanically damage an operative default trigger and require textual reconstruction.

judgments.title: Incomplete text in default provisions
judgments.reason: The garbled phrases “promis: us” and “tot! ander” mechanically obscure two operative default events.

judgments.title: No cure period before default acceleration
judgments.reason: Immediate contractual default and acceleration can coexist with a late fee imposed only after ten days; the provisions govern different consequences and do not conflict.

judgments.title: Formatting artifact in DEFAULT clause
judgments.reason: The OCR artifacts mechanically corrupt the identification of the Agreement and the payment-default trigger.

judgments.title: Formatting artifacts in DEFAULT obligations
judgments.reason: The multiple corruptions obscure the promises and lender obligations whose breach triggers default, as well as the consequence introduced by “If you default.”

judgments.title: Spelling error: "aotices"
judgments.reason: “Aotices” is plainly a misspelling of “notices” and does not alter the waiver’s scope.

judgments.title: Broad waiver of notices disadvantages customer
judgments.reason: The broad waiver of notices presents a substantive consumer-protection concern, not a textual construction defect.

judgments.title: Unilateral right to renew or extend obligations
judgments.reason: The unilateral renewal or extension authority is broad and unfavorable but unambiguous.
